data.heading: Visiting a synagogue for the first time
data.body:
If you've never been to a synagogue service, you're very welcome at [Synagogue Name]. Here's what to expect.

It's helpful to contact us before your first visit. [Describe any security check-in or entry procedures here.]

When you arrive, a greeter will welcome you and offer a prayer book. Kippot (head coverings) are available at the entrance. [Edit for your community's customs.]

Services include prayers, songs and readings, some in Hebrew and some in English. [Describe your prayer book and whether it has transliteration.] It's fine to follow along quietly, stand and sit with everyone else, or simply listen.

On Shabbat morning, the Torah scroll is taken out and read. It's a special moment in the service, and many people stand as it's carried through the room.

After services there's often a kiddush or oneg, a time for blessings over wine or grape juice and bread, food and conversation. [Edit for your community.] It's a great chance to meet people.

Please ask before taking photos or using your phone. [Add your community's guidance for Shabbat.]

We look forward to welcoming you.

data.heading: The Jewish holidays through the year
data.body:
The Jewish calendar is full of holidays, each with its own customs, foods and stories. Here's a short guide to the ones we celebrate together at [Synagogue Name].

The year begins with the High Holy Days: Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year, and Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, a day of fasting and reflection. [Add how to register for services.]

Soon after comes Sukkot, when people eat and gather in a sukkah, a temporary outdoor hut. In winter, Hanukkah, the festival of lights, is celebrated by lighting the menorah for eight nights.

Purim, in early spring, is a joyful festival with costumes and the reading of the Megillah. Then comes Passover, when families and friends gather for a seder to retell the story of the Exodus.

Because the Jewish calendar follows the moon, holiday dates move each year on the everyday calendar. We post dates and times on our events page.

Everyone is welcome to join our holiday celebrations. Check the events page for this year's dates.
